item.title: Claude and OpenAI Publish Proofs of VP ≠ VNP, GPT-6 Advances in Science and Code
item.description:
Claude and OpenAI Publish Proofs of VP ≠ VNP, GPT-6 Advances in Science and Code

An internal Claude research model reportedly provided a proof that VP ≠ VNP, which Anthropic shared in a GitHub repository. OpenAI subsequently posted its own proof, claiming it was ‘obtained on November 6, 2026’. The result does not imply P ≠ NP, which still requires general Boolean circuit lower bounds. Levent Alpöge noted that the ‘250,000+ pages’ claim was a joke.

OpenAI released a preprint showing GPT-6 models designed new protein shapes and sequences through reasoning and code, without specialized bio models. In one run, GPT-6 Cyber helped validate 948 Linux kernel bugs that could grant local root and generated patches for maintainer review. A historian reported that GPT-6.2 Astra identified the vicomte de Chabot as the artist of an anonymous 1808 Yale sketchbook in 22 minutes, and it also surfaced an obscure microfilmed diary whose handwriting and itinerary matched the sketches. Additionally, one 13.8-day signal was independently confirmed by a SETI astronomer, and 49 TESS candidates were flagged.

GPT-6.2 Astra on Codex scored 97% on RoboDojo-RC Tier 1 across 120 real-robot trials, with RoboDojo being retired. Einsia released RoboUniverse-10K, a set of 10,807 verifiable Isaac Sim tasks built from real manipulation videos, with a top frontier score of 85.8% and 7 of 11 models scoring ≤10%. Neon set a Day-1 usage record on Google’s paid APIs, and Antigravity tokens/day rose 82% since Argon launched six weeks ago. Neon is now available to Google Workspace customers through the Gemini app, and Perplexity has passed 120B Neon tokens, doubling daily volume in 3 days with 36B on Monday.

One estimate places Neon xhigh roughly equal to Opus Max at $6.44 vs $10.04 per Artificial Analysis task. Several users report heavy ‘glazing’ and overcorrection when Neon is critiqued. Users describe Opus 5.6 being A/B-tested in Claude Code and chat as ‘quite a jump’ over 5.5. The model is pure-RL trained on Kimi K3 and reportedly approaches frontier models on FrontierCode 2.0 at max reasoning, and is free on Devin paid tiers for two weeks.

GLM-5.4 creates five looped models in Raschka’s architecture gallery. The model runs its middle 24 of 32 layers twice and beats Qwen3.8-27B on GAIA (69.90 vs 66.99). It is about 4.9 GB at 4-bit and released under Apache 2.0. LoopCD contrasts loop pass 3 against pass 1 with no training, lifting AA-Omniscience from -9.0 to -3.4. Reported scores include #1 under 32B on DeepSWE (48.2%) and 79.2% on SWE-bench Verified. Unsloth fine-tuning of the model is up to 3x faster with 50% less VRAM.

#AI #OpenAI #Claude #GPT-6 #VP-not-VNP #ProteinDesign

Source: Gemini 4 Neon marks GDM’s full return as a Frontier Lab — Latent Space

item.title: GPT-6 Designs Proteins Using Reasoning and Code
item.description:
GPT-6 Designs Proteins Using Reasoning and Code

OpenAI has demonstrated that its GPT-6 family of models can design new protein shapes and amino acid sequences using only reasoning and code, eliminating the need for specialized biology models to generate designs.

🔍 Overview

The development is detailed in a preprint titled “GPT-6 as a Universal Foundation Model for Protein Biology: Beyond Specialized Models.” This work shows that GPT-6 possesses intrinsic capabilities for designing new proteins, allowing it to generate structures and sequences without relying on external, specialized biology tools. The approach simplifies the workflow by using general-purpose coding and reasoning instead of coordinating multiple specialized models.

🧩 How it works

Proteins are chains of amino acids whose order determines their three-dimensional shape and function. GPT-6 models approach this by leveraging knowledge from math, physics, chemistry, and biology to reason about protein shapes and molecular interactions.

  • Prompting and Guidance: Researchers can guide designs by specifying where a protein should attach and what shape it should take. This allows for control ranging from a single bond between two atoms to the overall protein shape.
  • Task Flexibility: Models can switch between tasks—such as designing minibinders, building proteins around specific features, or predicting interactions—simply by changing the prompt, without requiring retraining.
  • Comparison to Specialized Models: While specialized models require substantial expertise and specific inputs, GPT-6 uses general-purpose coding. Internal tests showed that GPT-6 models performed comparably to or better than specialized models on most design tasks, although predicting a complete protein structure remained a clear weakness.

⚙️ Key details

Laboratory tests conducted with research partner Onava validated the computational designs.

  • Minibinder Design: For five target proteins, Onava created small proteins based on GPT-6.2’s 3D structures. In each case, at least one protein showed evidence of binding to its intended target.
  • Antibody and Minibinder Resequencing: GPT-6.2 designed new amino acid sequences for existing minibinders and antibodies. These redesigned molecules retained their binding capabilities in lab tests.
  • Ligand Docking: GPT-6.2 was asked to predict where and how a small molecule would bind to a protein, a task it accomplished by switching prompts without retraining.
Model Performance vs. Specialized Models (RFdiffusion)
GPT-6.2 Scored slightly lower on 3D design quality
Latest Internal Models Scored higher than specialized models

💡 Why it matters

Specialized biology models often have rigid input constraints and require changes to software or additional training to accept new types of information. GPT-6’s ability to handle diverse protein biology tasks through prompt changes and general reasoning suggests a more flexible approach to protein design. This capability allows researchers to guide designs with high fidelity, such as specifying the number of coils or strands in a minibinder, with internal models following such instructions with near-perfect fidelity in 3D designs.

#GPT-6 #ProteinDesign #OpenAI #Bioinformatics #AIResearch

Source: GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities

item.title: NVIDIA releases RFD4-Proteina, an open BioNeMo model for joint protein sequence and structure design
item.description:
NVIDIA releases RFD4-Proteina, an open BioNeMo model for joint protein sequence and structure design

NVIDIA released RFD4-Proteina, an open BioNeMo model co-developed with the University of Washington’s Institute for Protein Design, that jointly designs protein sequences and all-atom structures using reward-guided inference-time search.

🔍 Overview

  • Co-developed with Institute for Protein Design at UW School of Medicine.
  • Uses patterns learned from nature to navigate protein design space.
  • Co-designs sequences and all-atom structures.
  • Employs reward-guided inference-time search to focus compute on promising candidates.

🧩 How it works

  • Combines explicit backbone coordinates with latent representation, learned sequence and atomistic variables.
  • Autoencoder decoder outputs sequence and all-atom structure together, removing need for separate inverse-folding step (e.g., ProteinMPNN).
  • During inference-time reasoning search, model denoises generation trajectories, scores designs, retains/branches promising partial states, continues until criteria met.
  • Rewards can measure geometry, interactions, or independent prediction confidence.
  • Uses residue-level latent representation (vs atom-level) to avoid memory blow-up.
  • Diffusion process engineered to cut sampling steps from ~400 (Proteina-Complexa) to ~60, focusing compute where reasoning matters.
  • Inference-time search accelerated via CUDA-accelerated oracles (OF3, physics methods like tmol).
  • Model and kernels co-designed with cuEquivariance and BioNeMo Inference Runtime (BIR) teams for speed/scalability.
  • AtomWorks provides molecular data layer for structure preparation and design annotations.

⚙️ Key details

  • Supports Linux GPU host, Python 3.12; follow repo setup guide, need supported NVIDIA GPU.
  • Self-host requirements: x86_64 or arm64 Linux meeting NIM prerequisites, Docker, NVIDIA Driver, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, NGC API key.
  • NIM API endpoint (not for production): HTTP via build.nvidia.com, Shell/Python scripts, no local GPU/model install.
  • Accepts annotated CIFs or condition specification plus source structure.
  • Uses repository’s cropped PD-L1 structure from PDB 5O45 as target; fix sequence/backbone, allow side-chain repack, direct binder generation to hotspot atoms Tyr56, Met115, Tyr123.
  • Generated binder length 100–150 residues, free sequence and coordinates.
  • Install repo environment with current uv release (validated 0.12.24); update uv if present to recognize CUDA 13.2.
  • Setup caches Hugging Face model bundle including paired autoencoder.

🚀 Availability

  • Available as open model for training, inference, method development, direct control over sampling code.
  • Also available as NIM microservice for rapid inference deployment with HTTP interface.

💡 Why it matters

  • Faster and uses less memory than prior RFD3 due to residue-level latent representation, reduced diffusion steps, CUDA-accelerated oracles, and co-designed kernels.
  • Enables efficient protein binder design with integrated sequence-structure generation.

#ProteinDesign #BioNeMo #NVIDIA #DrugDiscovery

Source: Design Proteins with RFD4-Proteina Using Reward-Guided Inference-Time Search | NVIDIA Technical Blog
